topic: Terraform remote state on S3 with locking
title: Day 85/100: Terraform Remote Backends and Locking
description:
Terraform state is the file that maps your code to real infrastructure. In this video you'll see why local state breaks the moment a second engineer joins, and how to move it to a remote backend with locking.

It's for engineers who already run terraform apply and want a setup that survives teams, CI pipelines and laptop failures.

sections.heading: Why state matters
sections.narration: Every time you run terraform apply, Terraform writes down what it created. That record is the state file. It maps each resource in your code to a real object in your cloud account. Lose it, and Terraform forgets what it built. It will try to create everything again, and that usually ends with errors or duplicate resources. So the first rule is simple. Treat state like production data.
bullets: State maps code to real resources

sections.heading: Move state to a remote backend
sections.narration: Local state lives on one laptop, so nobody else can safely run Terraform. A remote backend fixes that. On AWS, the common choice is an S3 bucket with versioning turned on. Versioning matters, because it lets you roll back a bad state write. Here is the backend block. Notice the use lockfile setting. It tells Terraform to create a lock file in the same bucket, so two people can't apply at the same time.

sections.heading: Recap and next step
sections.narration: Let's recap. State is the memory of your infrastructure. Keep it remote, versioned, encrypted and locked. Your next step is to migrate one existing project with terraform init and the migrate state flag. Do it on a small project first, and keep a backup of the old file until you're confident.

code.content:
terraform init -migrate-state
terraform plan   # expect: No changes

short.title: Day 85/100: Your Terraform state is not a backup
short.hook: Delete this file and Terraform forgets everything.
short.narration: Delete this file and Terraform forgets everything. It's called the state file, and it maps your code to the real resources in your cloud. If it only lives on your laptop, your team can't work safely and one disk failure wipes the map. Store it in a remote backend like S3, turn on versioning, and enable locking so two applies never collide. Full video on the channel.
